context.why: Story 1 is accepted. fairdm/api/serializers.py now has PersonListSerializer (url, html_url, uuid, name, given_name, family_name, identifiers, primary_organization), OrganizationListSerializer, OrganizationReferenceSerializer ({uuid, url, name}) and the rewritten credit serializers. fairdm/api/viewsets.py has PersonViewSet over Person.objects.real() and OrganizationViewSet, both read-only and both serving the LIST serializer for the single record too. tests/test_api/test_viewsets.py has TestPeopleList for the list entry. This story gives a single person its fuller serializer, adds the people filters, and documents both. The moved test TestContributor.test_a_person_is_returned_with_what_their_profile_page_shows lost its assertions on profile and links in story 1 (decisions.md D14): T009 brings them back on the single record.
spec_sections: Clarifications (what the API may say about a person; list entry versus single record)
FR-004 to FR-008, FR-021 to FR-025
Edge Cases (primary affiliation ended; identifier with no resolver)
prior_decisions: decisions.md D9: PersonSerializer returns alternative_names and each affiliation's type although the person's own page does not show them today. Keep both exactly as plan D2 lists them and add nothing beyond that list.
PersonSerializer(PersonListSerializer) adds exactly: alternative_names, profile, links, languages, image, affiliations. Do NOT add `projects` or `datasets` here; story 4 adds them with their filter.

`links` and `languages`: the removed ContributorSerializer gave links as a list of addresses from contributor.get_links_display() and languages as names from contributor.get_language_names(); look at commit 36d9049c:fairdm/api/serializers.py lines 644-722 with `git show` and keep those two shapes.

`affiliations` comes from Person.get_affiliation_history(): current first (primary first), then past. Each entry is exactly {organization: {uuid, url, name}, type, start, end, is_primary}. `type` is the lower-case name of Affiliation.MembershipType (member, admin, owner); a pending affiliation never appears because get_affiliation_history() leaves it out. `start` and `end` are the partial dates as recorded, using Affiliation.start_display and end_display, with null (not an empty string) when unset.

PersonViewSet.get_serializer_class() returns PersonListSerializer for the list action and PersonSerializer otherwise. The queryset already prefetches identifiers and affiliations__organization; get_affiliation_history() reads that cache, so the single record and the list add no query per affiliation.

PersonFilterSet in fairdm/api/filters.py with two filters. `organization`: a ModelChoiceFilter matching Organization by uuid (to_field_name='uuid'), narrowing to people with an affiliation to it whose type is at least MEMBER and whose end_date is null; a database number is refused with a 400 as the other uuid filters do. `identifier`: IdentifierFilter, a django_filters.CharFilter subclass also in filters.py, which trims the value, strips a known scheme address from the front (the values of IdentifierLookup in fairdm/contrib/contributors/choices.py, matching with and without a trailing slash and with http or https), and matches identifiers__value exactly or with its spaces removed. Use .distinct() where a join could repeat a person.

FairDMFilterBackend (filters.py) builds each list's filter set from the view's filterset_class plus ChangedSinceFilterSet; set filterset_class on PersonViewSet and read how get_filterset_class combines them before choosing the Meta of PersonFilterSet (model Person, fields []).
Hidden accounts: the people list is Person.objects.real(), so an identifier a superuser holds returns an empty list (T010) with no extra code. Test it anyway.

T009's last assertion walks every people response, list and single record, at any depth, for a key that names account state. Use an explicit set of forbidden keys (email, password, is_staff, is_superuser, is_active, is_claimed, last_login, date_joined, groups, user_permissions, portal_roles, config, synced_data, last_synced, added, modified) so the test fails if a field is added later.

T013: tests/test_api/test_schema.py already has tests for how viewsets are described; add that the people list operation's response component and the single person's component each list their own fields (the single one has affiliations, the list one does not) and that the list operation documents the `organization` and `identifier` parameters. docs/portal-development/restful-api.md already has a short People section from story 1: extend it with the single person's fields in a table, what the list leaves out, the two filters with one example request each, and one sentence on what is never returned. Name PersonSerializer, PersonFilterSet and IdentifierFilter in the serializer reference table or beside it.
